newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo's Tehnogas mulls sale to foreign firms-paper.
newsitem.headline: Yugo's Tehnogas mulls sale to foreign firms-paper.

text.p: Tehnogas, Yugoslavia's biggest producer and distributer of industrial gases, could soon sell a majority stake to a foreign partner, Belgrade daily Nasa Borba reported Tuesday.

Tehnogas, the value of which has been estimated at 46 million German marks, has been in talks for some time now with three leading world companies in the field, Tehnogas Assistant General Manager Dobrivoje Popovic was quoted as saying.
The three are France's Lear Liquid and Messer and Linde of Germany.

The firms are already present in other former Yugoslav countries -- Meser in Zagreb, Croatia and Ljubljana, Slovenia and Linde in Karlovac, Croatia -- where they have purchased stakes in local companies, Popovic said.
"We are late but we hope to succeed in finding a common interest with a foreign partner," he added.

Tehnogas is yet to decide on its privatisation model, but industry sources saw it opting for a capitalisation issue, after which the new foreign partner would be able to acquire more than 50 percent stake in the firm, Popovic said.
The bulk of the capital raised through privatisation would be used for technological and technical upgrading.
The rest would be used to settle the problem of surplus labour, estimated at around 30 percent, some of whom will be retrained and others retired, Popovic said.
But the entire process will be gradual and could last up to five years, he added.

Tehnogas sells most of its products locally, but since its capacities were built for a much wider market of the ex-Yugoslavia, foreign partners might be interested in exports to neighbouring countries as well, Popovic said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
